These findings provide novel evidence for a differential facial emotion processing in dancers, extending the dance expertise modulation beyond perception of dance-specific stimuli, to face emotion perception. Overall, this work highlights the strong influence of sensorimotor training on emotion perception.

title: Cell-type specific and nanoscale control of hippocampal presynaptic homeostatic plasticity.
abstract: The lifelong continuity of neuronal function rests upon the perdurance of neurons, synapses and neural circuits that are sustained, in part, by homeostatic signaling. Currently, the implementation of homeostatic signaling within complex brain circuitry remains poorly defined. Given the tremendous diversity of cell and synapse types, is homeostatic plasticity deployed in a cell-type specific manner and, if so, what are the rules? Here, we report that presynaptic homeostatic plasticity (PHP) is achieved in a target neuron-specific manner. PHP is robust at synapses that contact parvalbumin-positive (PV+) and absent at somatostatin-positive (SST+) interneurons. Furthermore, PHP can be differentially induced at adjacent synapses that are present within single axonal boutons, separated by hundreds of nanometers. These highly localized effects are eliminated in the absence of Sema3A signaling, a homeostatic signaling molecule. Our data suggest a model where PHP is repressed throughout axons that contact SST+ interneurons and locally de-repressed with nanoscale precision.

title: Neuroprotective Effect of Magnoflorine Through Inhibition of Caspase-3-Mediated Neuronal Apoptosis: In Silico to In Vitro Validation.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
abstract: Neurodegeneration is a progressive biological phenomenon that is significantly driven by neuronal apoptosis. The current study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective potential of Magnoflorine, a natural alkaloid, by inhibiting Caspase-3-mediated neuronal apoptosis induced by Kainic acid. The caspase-3-inhibiting property of Magnoflorine was initially predicted using in silico methods such as molecular docking, MMGBSA analysis, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, taking Kainic acid as the reference neurotoxic ligand. Molecular docking and MMGBSA analysis showed that Magnoflorine has a higher binding affinity for caspase-3 than that of Kainic acid, which predicts the potential of Magnoflorine to inhibit caspase-3 expression. MD simulations further highlighted this potential through the greater stability of the Caspase-3-Magnoflorine complex than the Caspase-3-Kainic acid complex over 200 ns of simulations. It was finally evaluated through multiple in vitro techniques such as the MTT cell viability assay, LDH cytotoxicity assay, Annexin V-PI apoptosis assay, and immunocytochemistry performed on the retinoic acid-differentiated SH-SY5Y cells. MTT and LDH assays revealed that Magnoflorine significantly improved the viability of differentiated SH-SY5Y cells by reducing Kainic acid-induced cell death and cytotoxicity. The apoptosis assay also showed that Magnoflorine significantly reduced the Kainic acid-induced apoptosis in differentiated SH-SY5Y cells. Inhibition of Caspase-3 by Magnoflorine became evident during immunocytochemistry through the reversal of the Kainic acid-induced increase in Caspase-3 expression in differentiated SH-SY5Y cells, as observed from immunofluorescence intensity. The present study suggests that Magnoflorine is emerging as a valuable therapeutic agent for neurodegeneration by alleviating neuronal apoptosis, which requires further validation through in vivo studies.

title: Psychotropic Drug GST Interactions: In Vitro Inhibition, Molecular Docking, and Translational Potential in Cancer Therapy.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
abstract: Psychotropic drugs are widely used to treat mental disorders, but they also influence cellular pathways linked to cancer. One key enzyme, Glutathione S-transferase (GST), is involved in detoxification and drug resistance in tumors, making it a potential target in cancer therapy. This study examined the effects of selected psychotropic agents aripiprazole, fluoxetine hydrochloride, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate on GST activity derived from equine liver. Enzyme kinetics were assessed in vitro using 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) as the substrate and ethacrynic acid (Kᵢ = 4.7 ± 0.8 nM) as the standard reference inhibitor. IC50 values were determined, and inhibition constants (Kᵢ) were calculated via Lineweaver-Burk plot analysis. The ranked Kᵢ values were as follows: Haloperidol (2.80 ± 1.6 nM) < Ethacrynic acid (4.70 ± 0.8 nM) < Risperidone (4.90 ± 0.39 nM) < Fluoxetine hydrochloride (5.40 ± 1.0 nM) < Aripiprazole (6.10 ± 0.7 nM) < Sodium valproate (386.0 ± 0.0 nM). Haloperidol showed the strongest GST inhibition among the tested drugs, even exceeding ethacrynic acid in binding affinity. This suggests its potential as a GST modulator in cancer therapy. Molecular docking studies revealed that the highest binding affinities were observed for Risperidone and Aripiprazole, showing scores of -7.350 to -7.576 Kcal/mol for 9GSS and -8.786 to -8.982 Kcal/mol for 5JCU. These strong interactions indicate a high potential of both compounds to effectively bind within the GST active site. The molecular dynamics simulation confirmed the stability and consistency of these complexes throughout the simulation period. Given the anticancer role of GST inhibitors, psychotropic drugs with significant GST inhibition especially haloperidol may positively contribute to cancer treatment.

title: Age and Neuroimmune Diseases.
abstract: With the aging population accelerating, age has become a core factor influencing the clinical phenotypes, treatment responses, and prognoses of neuroimmune diseases (NDs), including those affecting the central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral nervous system (PNS). This cross-disease review summarizes the shared and specific age-related characteristics of NDs, focusing on the pathological basis of immunosenescence and neurodegeneration underlying age-related ND progression. We extract the clinical manifestations, immune and neural mechanisms of elderly ND patients, and evaluate the challenges and individualized adjustment principles of therapeutic strategies for this population. We explore the age-related immune dysregulation features between NDs and other systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), type 1 diabetes (T1D)). This review aims to construct a cross-disease framework for the precision management of NDs in the aging era, identify research gaps and future directions, and emphasize age-adapted intervention strategies for optimizing the prognosis of elderly ND patients.

title: Antibacterial and pro-osteointegrative bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces for oromaxillofacial applications: a systematic review and bayesian network meta-analysis of preclinical studies.
abstract: Numerous preclinical studies have investigated bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces to enhance antibacterial and osteointegrative performance in oromaxillofacial applications. However, these studies employ heterogeneous experimental methods and biological outcomes, making it difficult to identify which coating strategies hold the greatest translational potential. This systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to rank titanium coating strategies published over the last five years according to their biological performance, using a quantitative statistical framework. Nine coating categories of increasing compositional complexity, ranging from single-component (inorganic, organic, peptides/growth factors) to two-component and three-component formulations combining these classes with each other or with antibiotics, were compared across six biological outcomes in preclinical models. Inclusion criteria followed the PICOS framework for studies published between 2020 and 2025. Three databases were searched according to PRISMA 2020 and its NMA extension. Mean difference (MD) was used for outcomes on a common scale; ratio of means (RoM) when measurement units were heterogeneous. Treatment ranking was estimated using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Study reporting quality and data completeness were assessed, and studies with insufficient quantitative data were excluded from the quantitative synthesis. Of 143 records identified, 59 met the inclusion criteria and 40 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. SUCRA rankings indicated that three-component hybrid coatings incorporating antibiotics achieved the highest antibacterial performance and osseointegration, while inorganic coatings functionalized with peptides or growth factors demonstrated superior osteogenic differentiation. Organic coatings combined with peptides or growth factors showed the greatest cell proliferation. These findings provide the first evidence-based ranking of bioactive coating strategies for titanium implant surfaces, suggesting a potential advantage of multi-component formulations over single-agent approaches across biological outcomes. The identified compositional complexity gradient may inform the rational design of future multifunctional coatings and help prioritize candidates for further preclinical and translational validation in oromaxillofacial applications.

title: Unleashing the potential of saturation-transfer MR fingerprinting (ST-MRF) in neuro-oncology: quantitative molecular CEST and MTC mapping.
abstract: Neuro-oncology biomarkers allow probing tissues beyond anatomical or relaxation contrast. However, new techniques are needed to achieve mechanistic elucidation and effective therapeutic interventions. Quantitative MRI techniques, such as T1, T2, diffusion, and perfusion imaging, provide insights into tumor biology, infiltration, microstructure, and hemodynamics, and have been implemented clinically, but are limited in probing cellular and molecular changes. Saturation transfer (ST) MRI methods, including magnetization transfer contrast (MTC) and chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST), exhibit enhanced sensitivity to semisolid macromolecular content, mobile proteins, tissue metabolites, and acidosis. Despite these advantages, ST-MRI techniques typically have been qualitative or semi-quantitative, time-consuming, and impractical for clinical implementation. However, emerging ST-MR fingerprinting (ST-MRF) represents a significant analytical advancement by integrating RF saturation preparation into a pseudo-randomized MRF acquisition framework with a deep learning-based reconstruction. This approach enables simultaneous, clinically realistic, quantitative mapping of bulk water relaxation properties (e.g., T1 and T2), semisolid macromolecular parameters, and exchangeable solute dynamics (e.g., pool size ratios and exchange rates). We provide a comprehensive background, methodological principles, and evolving clinical applications of ST-MRF in neuro-oncology. We explore current advancements, strengths, limitations, and future possibilities for clinical translation into neuro-oncology workflows, including tumor characterization, treatment response monitoring, infiltration mapping, and biomarker development.

title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
abstract: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke. In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter. Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047). GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings. A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

title: Reduced hypoxanthine Ameliorates LPS-triggered autism-like stereotyped behaviors in intestinal Tlr4 knockout mice via the DRN ROS-5-HT axis.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves social deficits and severe stereotyped behavior. While central serotonin (5-HT) systems and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) activation are known to be implicated in ASD, how gut TLR4 affects central 5-HT and stereotyped behavior remains unknown. This study demonstrated that prenatal lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced social deficits in offspring of both intestinal Tlr4 knockout (Tlr4△IEC) and Tlr4fl/fl mice. However, the stereotyped behaviors and the inhibition of dorsal raphe nuclei (DRN) 5-HT were reduced in Tlr4△IEC-LPS mice compared with those in Tlr4fl/fl-LPS mice. By intersecting metabolites present in both colonic and cerebrospinal fluid, and selecting those exclusively changing in the colon of Tlr4fl/floffspring, hypoxanthine was identified as a metabolite that can cross the blood-brain barrier and mediate the effects of intestinal Tlr4 knockout on DRN 5-HT signaling. Remarkably, hypoxanthine and xanthine oxidase were increased in the serum of ASD children compared to typical development (TD) children. In vivo and in vitro experiments confirmed that hypoxanthine increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reduced 5-HT production, thereby promoting 5-HT neuron apoptosis. The inhibition of both the PI3K/AKT and 5-HT pathways in H2O2-treated PC12 cells was rescued by glutathione pretreatment in vitro. Meanwhile, the above LPS-induced DRN changes were significantly different in the Tlr4fl/fl offspring, and were reversed in the Tlr4△IEC mice after LPS exposure. Collectively, intestinal Tlr4 knockout reduces LPS-induced stereotyped behaviors, and the mechanism involves reduced hypoxanthine production and ROS-mediated inhibition of PI3K/AKT signaling, thereby decreasing 5-HT neuronal apoptosis by elevating the 5-HT level in DRN.

title: Enhancing the Suppression of Unwanted Memories During NREM Sleep.
abstract: Memory suppression, the ability to exclude unwanted memories from awareness, plays a critical role in maintaining mental well-being. Whereas the mechanisms of memory suppression during wakefulness have been extensively studied, the effects of sleep on this process and its associated neural mechanisms remain understudied. Targeted memory reactivation, an experimental approach for investigating the relationship between sleep and memory processing, provides a unique opportunity to further explore this relationship. Here, we combined the Think/No-Think paradigm with targeted memory reactivation to investigate whether and how reactivating suppression processes during sleep engages its associated neural mechanisms and influences later memory performance. Participants first learned cue-associate word pairs. They were then presented with trials, each exposing a cue word, preceded by an auditory instruction requiring the participant to either retrieve or suppress the corresponding target word. Subsequently, during NREM sleep, we unobtrusively re-presented the auditory tone signaling the instruction to suppress retrieval. We found that cueing people to suppress in this manner significantly enhanced suppression-induced forgetting on a later post-sleep test, compared to pairs that were not cued during sleep. Electroencephalogram analyses revealed that reactivation of suppression instructions increased theta power and reduced the coupling strength between spindles and the slow oscillation (SO) up-states. Importantly, only reduced SO up-state-spindle coupling predicted poorer later memory retrieval for suppressed pairs. The present results suggest that the disruption of neural synchrony between SO up-state and spindles during sleep plays a critical role in enhancing subsequent suppression-induced forgetting.

title: Predictors of depressive symptom emergence and recurrence in youth at risk of mood disorders: Findings from the T-RAD study.
abstract: The prevalence of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) among adolescents has increased substantially, underscoring the need to identify predictors of onset. We investigated the associations between mood-related factors, resilience factors, and quality-of-life domains and emergence of elevated depressive symptoms in adolescents and young adults at risk for depression. Participants enrolled in the RAD arm of the Texas Resilience Against Depression (T-RAD) study (longitudinal, observational) were included in the current analysis. Depressive symptom emergence was defined as the first occurrence of a categorical score of mild, moderate, severe, or very severe depression as reported using the Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology - Self Report (IDS-SR), Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology Clinician Report (QIDS-C), and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between clinical assessments and the time to elevated symptom emergence. Among RAD study participants (n = 111), 44.1% (n = 49) reported elevated depressive symptoms in at least one visit in up to 7.7 years of study participation, with average time to symptom emergence of 0.78 years and a mean age at symptom emergence of 19.7 years. Among those who reported elevated depressive symptoms, 69.4% (n = 34) reported additional occurrence of elevated symptoms, with significantly lower baseline psychological quality-of-life scores (p = .02). Baseline anxiety, childhood emotional abuse, poor family connectedness, and low psychological health, were significantly associated with increased risk of experiencing elevated depressive symptoms (p < .05). Our preliminary findings highlight family connectedness and psychological well-being as prevention targets among at-risk youth. The RAD study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03458936).

title: Brain structural features of treatment resistant depression in a large Italian sample: A multimodal imaging study.
abstract: Major depressive disorder is a common psychiatric condition characterized by persistent low mood, emotional dysregulation, and cognitive impairments affecting daily functioning. Approximately 30% of patients fail to respond adequately to at least two antidepressant trials, a condition known as treatment resistant depression (TRD), the neurobiology of which is still poorly understood. This study therefore aimed to investigate grey matter (GM) and white matter (WM) alterations associated with treatment resistance, directly comparing patients with TRD, treatment-sensitive depression (TSD), and healthy controls (HCs). MRI data were acquired from 294 individuals with MDD (193 TRD and 101 TSD) and 72 HCs. Group differences were assessed using analyses of variance followed by post-hoc t-tests. Compared with TSD patients, TRD patients showed reduced GM volume in striatal, temporal, and medial orbitofrontal regions. Relative to HCs, TSD patients exhibited localized GM reductions in the anterior cingulate cortex, whereas TRD patients showed extensive reductions across frontal, temporal, parietal, and limbic areas. Significant differences also emerged in WM microstructural integrity, as measured by fractional anisotropy (FA), axial diffusivity (AD), radial diffusivity (RD), and mean diffusivity (MD). Compared with both TSD patients and HCs, TRD patients exhibited widespread FA reductions paralleled by increased AD, RD, and MD values, whereas no significant differences emerged between TSD patients and HCs. These findings provide evidence that TRD is characterized by a distinct neurobiological profile, offering new insights into the mechanisms of treatment resistance that may ultimately facilitate the development of more effective, tailored therapeutic interventions.

title: Peripheral Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Changes and Clinical Response to Electroconvulsive Therapy and Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading contributor to the global burden of disease, and a substantial proportion of patients experience inadequate responses to conventional treatments. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a key regulator of neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, has been investigated as a potential biomarker of antidepressant response. However, its clinical relevance following brain stimulation remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated changes in peripheral BDNF concentrations and their association with clinical outcomes following electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in adults with MDD. The review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, and searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online), PsycINFO, and LILACS (Latin America and the Caribbean Literature on Health Sciences). Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved through consensus or consultation with a third reviewer. Eleven studies met the eligibility criteria, including two randomized controlled trials and nine non-randomized investigations. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a meta-analysis was not performed, and findings were synthesized narratively. Peripheral BDNF responses varied across interventions, biological matrices, and sampling intervals. While many studies reported increased serum or plasma BDNF following ECT, others documented substantial clinical improvement without corresponding biomarker changes. Evidence following rTMS was less consistent, with insufficient data to establish a reliable association between BDNF changes and antidepressant response. Overall, peripheral BDNF changes did not consistently parallel clinical improvement, and current evidence does not support their use as a standalone biomarker of antidepressant response. Further adequately powered studies with standardized biomarker measurements and longitudinal clinical assessments are warranted.

title: Mapping intratumoral heterogeneity in adolescent CNS tumors using simultaneous amide proton transfer-weighted signal and 18F-choline PET: A feasibility study.
abstract: Pediatric and adolescent gliomas and glioneuronal tumors remain challenging to assess noninvasively. Amide proton transfer (APT) chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) MRI has shown promise in adult gliomas but has not been well studied in younger patients. We conducted a feasibility study to assess whether APT-weighted signal can act as a noninvasive surrogate of tumor proliferation in adolescent central nervous system (CNS) tumors by correlating it with 18F-choline PET uptake (standardized uptake value [SUV]) as a proxy for membrane synthesis/proliferative activity. Ten adolescent patients (14-19 years), seven with histologically confirmed and three with radiologically suspected CNS tumors, underwent simultaneous APT-CEST and 18F-choline PET-MRI. Regions of interest (ROIs) corresponding to nonenhancing, enhancing, necrotic tumor, and contralateral white matter were delineated. Mean APT-weighted signal intensity and PET SUV were extracted per ROI. Nonparametric statistics and Spearman's correlation analyses were performed. APT-weighted signal was significantly elevated in enhancing, nonenhancing, and necrotic tumor ROIs compared to normal white matter (P < .001). 18F-choline SUV was elevated in enhancing and necrotic ROIs vs white matter, but not significantly so for nonenhancing tumor (P = .02). A correlation between enhancing and whole-tumor APT-weighted signal and 18F-choline SUV was seen (P < .001). This pilot feasibility study demonstrates that APT-CEST MRI is technically feasible in adolescents with CNS tumors and that APT-weighted signal may reflect tumor metabolic activity. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, histologically homogeneous cohorts. The detection of elevated APT-weighted signal even in nonenhancing tumor regions suggests potential utility in monitoring noncontrast-enhancing disease. Larger cohorts and multimodal correlation (eg Ki-67, amino acid PET) are warranted to confirm and extend these findings.

title: AIM-Photonics Visible-to-Near-Infrared Silicon-Nitride-Based Silicon-Photonics Platform and Component Library.
abstract: Silicon-photonics platforms operating at visible and near-infrared wavelengths are essential for a growing range of applications, including biosensing, chemical detection, Raman spectroscopy, quantum, optogenetics, and displays. However, unlike their infrared counterparts, visible-wavelength platforms have lacked comprehensive component libraries with pre-characterized devices, limiting the ability to rapidly design photonic integrated circuits for these applications. In this work, we present the design, fabrication, and broadband experimental characterization of a comprehensive visible-to-near-infrared-spanning component library for the AIM-Photonics 300-mm-wafer silicon-nitride-based platform, which features two silicon-nitride waveguiding layers, a sensing trench, thermo-optic phase shifters for modulation, and a dicing trench for fiber-to-chip edge coupling. We design and characterize components for both the fundamental quasi-transverse-electric and quasi-transverse-magnetic modes for wavelengths spanning from 450 to 1000 nm. To enable this characterization, we utilize a spectrum-spanning broadband measurement setup and methodology. The component library includes passive waveguides, edge couplers, grating couplers, multimode-interferometer splitters, directional couplers with varying splitting ratios, waveguide crossings, interlayer-transition escalators, polarization rotators, polarization splitters, sensing-trench components, and thermo-optic phase shifters. This work provides a foundry-compatible pre-characterized library of photonic building blocks that enables the rapid design and deployment of visible-to-near-infrared photonic integrated circuits for sensing, quantum, biomedical, display, and other emerging applications.

title: RiboMeth-Sequencing Reveals Selective Ribosomal RNA 2'-O-Methylation Changes in the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex of Subjects With Major Depressive Disorder.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with widespread molecular abnormalities in the brain; however, the contribution of ribosome-centered regulatory mechanisms remains poorly understood. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) 2'-O-methylation (Nm) is the most abundant and evolutionarily conserved RNA modification and has emerged as a determinant of ribosome heterogeneity and translational control. However, the rRNA Nm landscape has not been examined in psychiatric illness. Here, we used RiboMeth-seq to map site-specific rRNA Nm in the MDD brain. RiboMeth-seq was performed in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of individuals with MDD (n = 17) and matched nonpsychiatric control subjects (n = 20) using an Illumina NextSeq2000 in 50-bp single-end mode. Specific RiboMeth-seq scores were calculated in ±2 nucleotide intervals for all RNA positions and extracted for the positions of known Nm residues in target RNA. The overall distribution of ribose methylation scores was highly similar between groups, indicating the preservation of the global rRNA Nm landscape in MDD. At the same time, we identified 8 significantly altered Nm sites, including 4 in 28S rRNA (Am2802, Cm2848, Cm3866, and Gm4593) and 4 in 18S rRNA (Um172, Am576, Am1031, and Gm1490). These selective changes occurred in the absence of widespread remodeling, supporting a model in which MDD is associated with targeted modification of functionally relevant ribosomal positions rather than a generalized disruption of ribosome integrity. Our findings identify rRNA Nm as a previously unrecognized layer of molecular alteration in MDD and suggest that site-specific variation in ribosome composition may contribute to aberrant translational regulation in the depressed brain.

title: Cardioprotective Effects of Low-Dose Bisoprolol Against Anthracycline-Induced Subclinical Cardiotoxicity in Breast Cancer: A Triple-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial Using Advanced Echocardiographic Parameters.
abstract: Anthracyclines are cornerstone agents in breast cancer chemotherapy. However, they can cause dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, potentially impairing long-term cardiac function. Beta-blockers have demonstrated cardioprotective effects. However, evidence regarding bisoprolol, particularly using comprehensive echocardiographic evaluations, remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the cardioprotective effects of low-dose bisoprolol against anthracycline-induced subclinical cardiac dysfunction in patients with breast cancer. This triple-blind, randomized controlled trial was conducted in Isfahan, Iran, between January and December 2023. Eligible women with locally advanced breast cancer receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy were randomized to bisoprolol (2.5 mg/day) or a placebo. Cardiac function was assessed at baseline, mid-treatment, and the end of treatment during a 6-month follow-up period. The evaluated echocardiographic parameters included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular end-diastolic and end-systolic dimensions (LVEDD, LVESD), left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), global longitudinal strain (GLS), and tricuspid annular systolic excursion (TAPSE). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software (version 25.0). Continuous variables were analyzed using paired or independent-samples t tests, and categorical variables were analyzed using the Chi square test. Statistical significance was defined as P<0.05. A total of 50 patients completed the trial (25 in the bisoprolol group and 25 in the placebo group). LVEF remained stable in both groups. Compared with the placebo group, bisoprolol demonstrated significantly more favorable structural and functional changes, including a reduction in LVEDD (mean change=-0.172 cm; 95% CI=-0.343 to -0.001; P=0.049), LVESD (mean change=-0.156 cm; 95% CI=-0.295 to -0.172; P=0.029), and LVEDV (mean change=-7.920 mL; 95% CI=-15.174 to -0.666; P=0.033); improved GLS (mean change=0.974; 95% CI=0.083 to 1.865; P=0.033); and better preserved TAPSE (mean change=0.168 cm; 95% CI=0.101 to 0.234; P<0.001). Prophylactic bisoprolol might attenuate early subclinical cardiotoxicity in patients with breast cancer receiving anthracyclines, primarily through the stabilization of LVEDV and a more favorable GLS trajectory.Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials: IRCT20130701013828N8.

title: Limited prediction of self-rated performance in elite female footballers.
journal: International journal of clinical and health psychology : IJCHP
abstract: Routine athlete monitoring captures psychological and physical states across training and match cycles. Whether these indicators distinguish subsequent self-rated match performance below an athlete's own prior ratings remains uncertain. This retrospective exploratory prediction study examined whether match-day minus one (MD-1) monitoring indicators identified below-baseline self-ratings of overall team performance and of each player's own offensive and defensive performance among elite female footballers competing in Norway. SoccerMon provided 207 player-match records from 30 elite female footballers in two Toppserien clubs during 2020-2021. Requiring at least three strictly earlier match reports retained 124 records from 25 players. Psychological-behavioural, physical-status and joint predictor sets were evaluated using logistic regression and XGBoost. Below-baseline ratings were more than 0.50 points below the historical mean. Player-grouped validation used nested threshold selection. Average precision (AP) was the primary metric. Below-baseline prevalence was 31.5%, 26.6% and 32.3% for team, offensive and defensive ratings. The joint logistic reference model yielded AP values of 0.450 (95% CI 0.346-0.570), 0.308 (0.245-0.409) and 0.280 (0.241-0.363), respectively; ROC-AUCs were 0.590, 0.496 and 0.401. High false-discovery proportions limited classification utility. Discrimination was limited and inconsistent. These findings do not support clinical assessment, athlete selection or applied decision use. Individual historical references provide a transparent exploratory outcome definition; objective performance validity and transportability require direct investigation.

title: Microbiome-Derived Metabolites in Multiple Sclerosis: Mechanisms of Immune Regulation and Therapeutic Potential: A Literature Review.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune neuroinflammatory disease characterized by immune dysregulation, demyelination, and neurodegeneration of the central nervous system (CNS). Increasing evidence suggests that gut microbiota and microbiome-derived metabolites play important roles in the pathogenesis and progression of MS by modulating the gut-brain-immune axis. This narrative review examines the possible immunomodulatory effects of microbiome-derived metabolites in MS, with particular emphasis on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan-derived metabolites, and polyamines, and evaluates their potential therapeutic implications. This review was conducted using the most recent available studies relevant to the topic. The search included PubMed, Google Scholar, and PMC databases. Eligible studies focused on randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, observational studies, reviews, and other publications that examined the role of microbiota and its metabolites in MS. The reviewed evidence indicates that MS-associated dysbiosis is accompanied by altered microbial metabolite production, disruption of regulatory T cell (Treg)/T helper 17 (Th17) balance, impaired barrier integrity, and increased neuroinflammation. SCFAs, tryptophan-derived metabolites, and polyamines demonstrate immunoregulatory effects through modulation of T-cell responses, cytokine signaling, and inflammatory pathways. Microbiota-targeted interventions, including probiotics, prebiotics, dietary modulation, and metabolite supplementation, have shown promising immunological and clinical effects. However, methodological heterogeneity, small cohorts, variable interventions, and insufficient long-term clinical validation limit definitive conclusions regarding therapeutic efficacy. Future large-scale longitudinal and multi-omics studies are crucial for clarifying the underlying mechanisms and unlocking microbiota-targeted strategies to manage MS more effectively.
